description:
## What

Implement `pkix_aia::NoAiaFetcher` per PKIX-zkjb constraint 4. Zero-cost default that always returns `AiaError::FetchingDisabled`. Never panics.

```rust
pub struct NoAiaFetcher;

impl AiaFetcher for NoAiaFetcher {
    fn fetch(&self, _uri: &str) -> Result<Vec<u8>, AiaError> {
        Err(AiaError::FetchingDisabled)
    }
    // batch_fetch uses default-impl, returns Vec of all FetchingDisabled
}
```

## Acceptance

- [ ] `pkix_aia::NoAiaFetcher` is a public unit struct with `impl AiaFetcher`
- [ ] Returns `AiaError::FetchingDisabled` for any URI
- [ ] No allocation in fetch (besides the Err return)
- [ ] Unit test: fetch returns Err(FetchingDisabled) regardless of URI
- [ ] Unit test: batch_fetch returns Vec of Err(FetchingDisabled), one per URI
- [ ] Doctest: usage as `verify_chain(chain, anchors, policy, verifier, revocation, &NoAiaFetcher)` (after PKIX-zkjb.6 lands)

## Out of scope

- Configurable default that fetches sometimes — that's a real fetcher (pkix-aia-http) or a caller-side wrapper, not NoAiaFetcher

## Cross-references

- PKIX-zkjb (parent, constraint 4)
- pkix-revocation::NoRevocation (existing default pattern reference)
notes:
[2026-05-13 do-beads loop escalation] PKIX-zkjb.4 surfaces as autonomous-ready, but cannot be implemented autonomously without prerequisite work that the bd dep graph appears to gate incorrectly:

PROBLEM:
- PKIX-zkjb.4 says 'Implement pkix_aia::NoAiaFetcher.' That requires:
  (a) pkix-aia crate exists in workspace — currently does NOT (no pkix-aia/ directory).
  (b) pkix_aia::AiaError type defined — PKIX-zkjb.2 (status: open).
  (c) pkix_aia::AiaFetcher trait defined — PKIX-zkjb.3 (status: open).
- PKIX-zkjb.4 has zero blocking deps in bd ('depends on PKIX-zkjb' parent-child only).
- Meanwhile, PKIX-zkjb.3 (the trait it would implement) shows as 'depends on .4, .5, .6, .7'. That's structurally backwards — the trait must exist before the impl. Confirmed by inspecting 'bd show PKIX-zkjb.3 --json'.
- PKIX-zkjb.2 shows 'depends on PKIX-zkjb.3' — meaning the AiaError type is gated on the trait, which is also backwards (you define the error before the trait that returns it).

INTERPRETATION (two readings):
(i) The dep graph was wired backwards by accident. Correcting it: .2 (no blockers, ready) → .3 (blocks on .2) → .4 (blocks on .3) → .9 (blocks on .4). Then .4 surfaces naturally after .3 closes.
(ii) The dep graph encodes 'parent .3 blocks on child .4 closing' as a semantic for 'parent epic closes when all children close'. But .3 isn't an epic — it's a task. And task-on-task 'depends on' in bd should mean 'blocker' per the existing parent-child convention used in PKIX-wlsr.6/.7.

RECOMMEND: (i) — fix the dep wiring. Re-wire to:
  bd dep remove PKIX-zkjb.2 PKIX-zkjb.3   # remove backward dep
  bd dep remove PKIX-zkjb.3 PKIX-zkjb.4   # remove backward dep
  bd dep remove PKIX-zkjb.3 PKIX-zkjb.5   # remove backward dep
  bd dep remove PKIX-zkjb.3 PKIX-zkjb.7   # remove backward dep
  bd dep add PKIX-zkjb.3 PKIX-zkjb.2      # .3 trait depends on .2 error type
  bd dep add PKIX-zkjb.4 PKIX-zkjb.3      # .4 impl depends on .3 trait
  bd dep add PKIX-zkjb.5 PKIX-zkjb.3      # .5 adapter depends on .3 trait
  bd dep add PKIX-zkjb.7 PKIX-zkjb.3      # .7 integration depends on .3 trait
  bd dep add PKIX-zkjb.9 PKIX-zkjb.4      # .9 Verifier 3-generic depends on .4
After the fix, the natural autonomous order is .2 → .3 → .4 → .9 (with .5 and .7 paralleling after .3).

NOT FIXING IN-LOOP because: (a) bd dep rewiring touches Mark's design intent, not just my bead's scope; (b) the inversion suggests this might actually be a pattern Mark deliberately used (e.g., a 'parent depends on children for closure-gating' that bd doesn't explicitly model); (c) AGENTS.md 'destructive action guardrails' covers rewiring of work products implicitly — confirming with Mark before re-pointing 4 dep edges is the conservative move.
